Giv (or Gew) is a character from the Shahnameh, which is a long epic poem written by the Persian poet Ferdowsi between c. 977 and 1010 CE. The Shahnameh is often considered the national epic of Iran and is one of the world's longest epic poems created by a single poet. 

In the Shahnameh, Giv is a knight and one of the main heroes serving under the epic Persian King Kay Kavus and his successors. He is shown as loyal, brave, generous, and honorable, and plays a significant role in many battles and events.

One of the most famous stories involving Giv is his mission to locate and rescue the Iranian prince, Kay Khusrau, who was hidden by his mother in the land of Turan. Giv is shown as an accomplished diplomat in this tale and his treatment of the Turan prince Afrasiyab has been praised as an example of honorable conduct.

Giv's family, especially his brother Tus and his son Bizhan, also play prominent roles in the Shahnameh. Giv eventually loses his life during the reign of King Goshtasp in a battle against the forces of Arjasp, the king of the Khazar.

His character is notable not only for his military prowess and bravery but also for his wisdom, righteousness, and dedication to his king and country.
